Petitioners have filed the petition, under Section 22 of the Workmen's Compensation At, for grant of compensation, on account of death of Shri Parkash Chand, during the course of employment, against the owner of car No. HP-22-A-4649 (hereinafter referred to as 'the vehicle in question') and Insurer of the vehicle in question.

as per the petition, was employed by respondent No. 1, as driver on the of vehicle in question,

However, the vehicle in question met with an accident at village Dhaunsi, Salogra, District Solan and Prakash Chand (driver) died on the same day.

His post-mortem was conducted at Civil Hospital,
Solan.

12. The appeal, so filed, by the Insurance rt Company, has been admitted, by this Court, on 30.9.2013, on the following substantial questions of law:
"1.Whether inspite of clear case set up by the claimants in the claim petition that deceased Sh. Parkash Chand was employed as a helper by the insured, the owner/
insured was entitled for the indemnification of the claim under motor insurance policy when no employer-employee relationship between the owner of vehicle and deceased was established on record for the purpose of and within the meaning of Motor Insurance policy ?
2.

Whether amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.6,00,000/- awarded to claimants is legal and justified as per provisions of the Employee's Compensation Act or claimants are entitled to only an amount of Rs.2,56,660/ alongwith interest ?
13. Perusal of the impugned award shows that the learned Commissioner, while deciding the claim of the petitioner, has applied the principle of M.V. Act.
14.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs. Mohd. Nasir and another, (2009) 2 SCC (Cri.) 987 has differentiated between the .
provisions of M.V. Act and the Act.

sentences.text:
The relevant paras 23 and 24 of the judgment are reproduced as under:-
"23.

Both, the 1923 Act and 1988 Act are beneficent legislation insofar as they provide for payment of of compensation to the workmen employed by the employers and/or by use of motor vehicle by the owner thereof and/or the insurer to the petitioners suffering permanent disability.
The amount of compensation is to be rt determined in terms of the provisions of the respective Acts.

Whereas in terms of the 1923 Act, the Commissioner who is a quasi-judicial authority, is bound to apply the principles and the factors laid down in the Act for the purpose of determining the compensation, Section 168 of the 1988 Act enjoins the Tribunal to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to be just.
24. Both the Acts aim at providing for expeditious relief to the victims of accident.
In these cases, the accidents took place by reason of use of motor vehicles.
Both the statutes are beneficial ones for the workmen as also the third parties.

The benefits United India Insurance Co. Ltd vs Leela Devi & Others on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132252503/
4 thereof are available only to the persons specified under the Act besides under the Contract of Insurance.

sentences.text: The statutes, therefore, deserve liberal construction.

The legislative intent contained therein is required to be interpreted with a view to give effect thereto."
(self emphasis supplied)

The Commissioner was bound to decide the quantum of compensation, as per the provisions of Act, in force, on the day of accident.

The learned Commissioner, in this case, has wrongly applied the principle of the M.V. Act,
whereas the petition should have been decided, as per the Act.
of 17.
The accident in question had taken place on 14.6.2008, and the monthly income of deceased, has rt been pleaded as Rs. 6000/- per month.
This factual position has been asserted in para-4 of the petition.
Respondent No.1, who is employer of deceased, has admitted this fact.

Petitioner No. 1, Leela Devi,
while appearing in the witness box, has also asserted the monthly income of her husband (deceased Prakash Chand) to be Rs. 6000/- per month.
18. The learned Commissioner has taken the salary of deceased as Rs. 6000/- per month, and the life expectancy of the deceased as 70 years.
Thus, compensation of Rs. 5,76,000/- with hike, has been awarded to the petitioners, by the learned Commissioner.
Thus, final compensation, which has been assessed by the learned Commissioner, in this case, is Rs. 6,00,000/-.

19. Monthly income of deceased Prakash Chand .
has been admitted to be Rs. 6000/-.

In such situation, the question, which arises for determination,
by this Court, is whether the said amount can be taken into of consideration.

According to Explanation-II, attached to Section 4 (I) of the Act, the monthly income of rt deceased shall be deemed to be Rs. 4000/- per month, irrespective of the pleadings and admissions of the salary of deceased as Rs. 6000/- per month.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in K.Sivaraman & others vs. P. Sathishkumar & anr., reported in (2020) 4 Supreme Court Cases 594, has categorically of reiterated the legal position by stating that prior to the Act 45 of 2009, by virtue of deeming provision rt Explanation II to Section 4, monthly wages of an employee were capped at Rs. 4,000/-, even where, an employee was able to prove the payment of a monthly wage in excess of Rs. 4000/-.

entities.text: K.Sivaraman & others vs. P. Sathishkumar & anr., reported in (2020) 4 Supreme Court Cases 594
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant paragraph 26 of the judgment is reproduced as under:
"26.Prior to Act 45 of 2009, by virtue of the deeming provision in Explanation II to Section 4, the monthly wages of an employee were capped at Rs 4000 even where an employee was able to prove the payment of a monthly wage in excess of Rs 4,000.
The legislature, in its wisdom and keeping in mind the purpose of the 1923 Act as a social welfare legislation did not enhance the quantum in the deeming provision, but deleted it altogether.

The amendment is in furtherance of the salient purpose which underlies the 1923 Act of providing to all employees compensation for accidents which occur in the course of and arising out of employment.
The objective of the amendment is to remove a deeming cap on the monthly income of an employee and extend to them compensation on the basis of the actual monthly wages drawn by them.
However, there is nothing to indicate that the Legislature intended for the benefit to extend to accidents that took place prior to the coming into force of the amendment."
24. Since, the compensation has not been assessed by the learned Commissioner, as per the Act, .

as such, the appeal, preferred by the Insurance Company is partly allowed, and the compensation payable to petitioners, is liable to be re-assessed as of under:
i) Income of deceased = Rs. 4000/- per month (50% of 4,000/- =Rs.2000/-p.m.
25. rt
